Chapter Summary 
• A well-rounded, varied diet of mostly 
unprocessed foods will provide many of the DVs 
recommended by the FDA. 
• High doses of water-soluble vitamins are 
excreted in the urine, although fat-soluble 
vitamins are stored in the tissues. High doses of 
fat-soluble vitamins can lead to toxicity and even 
death. 
• Certain disease states require higher vitamin and 
mineral intake, supplemented beyond dietary 
sources. 
• Vitamin-mineral supplements should be selected 
based on age, sex, and specific need. 
• Coenzyme and antioxidant properties are critical 
functions of vitamins and minerals. 
• Nutrition facts food labels and MyPlate can assist 
in choosing foods high in vitamins and minerals. 
• RDAs and DVs reflect current nutrient research.
